analysis:
Examined the two base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 12404-13586), covering the tail of one Gemma-4 prompt-contract vector, the json_schema vector and the start of long_prompt. These are public synthetic test vectors ("Public synthetic cache-parity input", "cache cache ..."), with no secrets, credentials, keys, attestation data or consumer content. The file_changes patch excerpt (truncated, but the range map is complete) shows head-side edits to the fixture: it adds an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} member to one vector's request and updates prompt_token_count, block_boundaries chain hashes and token_ids. The changes only regenerate golden vectors. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or routing logic changed in the supplied units.

Security relevance is limited to T-041 (the prefix-cache chain-hash and prompt-contract identity feeding cache keys). Changing the template input and chain hashes only alters the fixture expectations. Whether the provider and coordinator implementations that consume these vectors honor the new additional_context field and the resulting cache-key/prompt_contract_id semantics (for example, that enable_thinking cannot cause cross-tenant cache aliasing) is not visible here. The prompt_contract_id shown for the base-side vectors (7fa068ec...) is unchanged in the visible excerpts, while the patch shows a different id (8171fec3...) for the modified vector, which I treat as expected for a distinct contract. The corresponding Swift or Go code changes, if any, are in other batches. No regression is identified in these units. The head-side contents of the changed hunks were not supplied in full, so this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety. The next pass should confirm that the code consuming additional_context participates in the prompt contract and cache hashing consistently.
